MedCat.evidence_source: [/page/5/Text/10] Youth reported levels of depression were comparable between PTA and ISP groups at screening (PTA: M = 22.39, SD 7.78; ISP: M = 22.59, SD 8.95). Participants assigned to PTA showed greater reduction in depression symptoms from Time 1 to Time 2 compared with the ISP group, using the youth-reported primary outcome measure (MFQ). The effect size for betweengroup differences on youth-reported depressive symptoms at Time 2 (post-intervention) was .36 [95% CI: −.02, .73]. Compared to the ISP group, PTA youth also reported a greater reduction of internalizing symptoms on the BASC-2 from Time 1 to Time 2. Group × time interactions for measures of parent-reported depressive symptoms, and internalizing and externalizing problems based on parent and teacher report were not significant. [/page/5/Text/11] Youth in PTA showed greater increases in personal adjustment on two of three measures: sense of inadequacy and self-esteem. Academic outcomes, as measured by the school problems scale of the BASC, did not significantly differ by groups over time for teacher or child report. Compared to ISP participants, youth in PTA showed greater gains in social skills according to parent-report, but not teacher-report. Indicators of interpersonal [/page/6/Text/4] relationships, including parent-child communication, relations with parent, and interpersonal relations, were not significantly different by group across time.
